column1: Let’s see what Friedman’s hypothesis implies for the average propensity to consume. Divide both sides of his consumption function by Y to obtain APC 5 C/Y 5 aYP/Y. According to the permanent-income hypothesis, the average propensity to consume depends on the ratio of permanent income to current income. When current income temporarily rises above permanent income, the average propensity to consume temporarily falls; when current income temporarily falls below permanent income, the average propensity to consume temporarily rises.
